body.en: Arithmetic sequences add a constant; geometric sequences multiply by one. Summing their terms gives series — including the surprising fact that an infinite geometric series can have a finite total.
An arithmetic sequence has a common difference \( d \); a geometric sequence has a common ratio \( r \). Their \( n \)th terms are \( a_1+(n-1)d \) and \( a_1 r^{\,n-1} \).

Find the 10th term of the arithmetic sequence with \( a_1=2 \), \( d=3 \).

\[ a_{10}=2+(10-1)(3)=29. \]

Find the sum of \( 8+4+2+1+\cdots \)

Geometric with \( a_1=8 \), \( r=\tfrac12 \):

\[ S=\frac{8}{1-\tfrac12}=16. \]

caption.en: Discrete terms of arithmetic sequence \(a_n = 2 + (n - 1)(3) = 3n - 1\) lying along a line with constant slope equal to common difference \(d = 3\).

label.en: ▲ Algebra 2 Traps & Commandments — Sequences, Series & Binomial Theorem

body.en:
• Arithmetic vs. Geometric Recognition: Arithmetic sequences possess a constant difference \(d = a_n - a_{n-1}\) (linear growth); geometric sequences possess a constant ratio \(r = a_n / a_{n-1}\) (exponential growth). Never confuse the summation formulas!
  • Counting Terms in Sigma Notation: The number of terms in \(\sum_{k=m}^n a_k\) is \(n - m + 1\), not \(n - m\). For instance, \(\sum_{k=3}^8 a_k\) contains \(8 - 3 + 1 = 6\) terms.
  • Infinite Sum Existence Condition: The infinite geometric series formula \(S = \frac{a_1}{1 - r}\) converges if and only if \(|r| < 1\). If \(|r| \ge 1\), the series diverges and has no finite sum.
  • Binomial Coefficient Sign Alternation: In \((a - b)^n\), the negative sign is bound to \(b\): term \(k\) is \(\binom{n}{k} a^{n-k} (-b)^k = (-1)^k \binom{n}{k} a^{n-k} b^k\). Terms alternate signs, starting positive for \(k = 0\).

question.en: Find the coefficient of \(x^2\) in the expansion of \((3-2x)^5\).
In an arithmetic sequence, the 4th term is 17 and the 10th term is 47. Find the first term \(a_1\), the common difference \(d\), and the sum of the first 25 terms \(S_{25}\).

solution.en:
Using \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\):

\[a_4 = a_1 + 3d = 17,\]\[a_{10} = a_1 + 9d = 47.\]

Subtract the first equation from the second:

\[6d = 30 \implies d = 5.\]

Substitute \(d = 5\) into the first equation:

\[a_1 + 3(5) = 17 \implies a_1 = 17 - 15 = 2.\]

Find the sum of the first 25 terms using \(S_n = \frac{n}{2}[2a_1 + (n - 1)d]\):

\[S_{25} = \frac{25}{2}[2(2) + 24(5)] = \frac{25}{2}[4 + 120] = \frac{25}{2}(124) = 25 \times 62 = 1550.\]
